text: Rather, that is only one of several relevant factors, including: — “(1) the nexus between the allegedly defamatory statement (or other tort) at issue and the third party plaintiff's employment by the insured, and — “(2) the existence (or nonexistence) of a relationship between the employer and the third party plaintiff outside the employment relationship.” [Low v. Golden Eagle Ins. Co., supra, 104 CA4th at 314, 128 CR2d at 428-429 (emphasis in original)] [3:406 - 3:419] Reserved. 3. [3:420] Tort Claims Collateral to Employment Termination: Claims for wrongful termination are often accompanied by collateral tort claims. E.g., intentional or negligent misrepresentations (false promises of fair treatment, etc.); intentional or negligent infliction of emotional distress; invasion of privacy; defamation (in employment references), etc. An insurer will often deny coverage for such collateral tort claims for the same reasons it denies coverage for the wrongful termination itself: a.
